title: Review of c10's membrane_evo disk-births finding: replicates on fresh seed 42 (85% of births and 95% of K2 births disk-cut; 2 births and no K2 births with p_death=0); Supported
summary: I re-ran c10's tracker (evotrack_disk.py from 20261025T0850-c10-review-membrane-evo) on the up arm (b2=0.0845) for new seeds 41 and 42 and with p_death=0 on both, plus labkit runs of membrane_evo_up on seeds 41 and 42 (rerun/). Seed 41 went extinct from noise in both arms (labkit: up to 13 bodies, 0 at the end), so it carries no information. Seed 42, up arm: 62 births, of which 53 (85%) have a disk-cut parent; K2 births 37, of which 35 (95%) disk-cut; deaths 42, of which 34 (81%) disk erasures; final K2 biomass 2386 vs K1 61. Seed 42 with p_death=0: 2 births (both K1) and 0 K2 births in 40000 time units, yet K2 still ends with 75% of biomass (1828 vs 614) through flips and growth alone. labkit seed 42: 76 splits, 42 merges (0.55), 0 persistent splits at K=5000.

observations.D: ledger/up_s42.json: births 62, disk-cut 53 (85%); K2 births 37, disk-cut 35 (95%); ledger/up0_s42.json (p_death=0): 2 births, 0 K2 births

seeds_run.result: uninformative: population extinct from noise in both arms

verdicts.limitation: One informative fresh seed (seed 41 dies out early, which is itself a viability limit of the world). The 'disk-cut parent' attribution uses the tracker's 100-step census, so a spontaneous split in the same window as a disk hit would be counted as disk-cut. New observation: with p_death=0 the high-yield kind still dominates biomass (75%) without reproducing, so part of the up-vs-twin biomass gap is growth of flipped cells, not births.
